other_failure_modes.name: Imputation before cross-validation splitting
other_failure_modes.description: The agent computes the imputation statistic (median) on the entire training set before performing the K-Fold split. This leaks information from the validation folds into the training folds, which can lead to overly optimistic cross-validation scores.

other_failure_modes.name: Batch-dependent test predictions (Transductive ranking)
other_failure_modes.description: The agent applies rank normalization to the test predictions within each fold. This means a single test sample's prediction depends on the other samples present in the test batch, breaking the assumption of independent predictions and making the model entirely unsuitable for single-instance inference in production.

summary: The agent implements a generally strong pipeline with domain-specific feature engineering, Stratified K-Fold cross-validation, and an ensemble of five tree-based models. However, it suffers from cross-validation leakage due to imputing missing values before splitting, uses a manually weighted ensemble without any tuning, and applies rank normalization to test predictions, which critically makes inference batch-dependent.
